General requirements:

1. Duly accomplished Application Form for Special Temporary Permit (STP) (The form is available at the https://www.prc.gov.ph/special-temporary-permits)

2. Photocopy of the data page of the valid passport as proof of citizenship (The validity of the passport must be within the duration of the practice of profession.)

3. Authenticated or Apostilled Professional license issued by the competent regulatory authority in his/her country with official English Translation thereof when necessary. For foreign Physicians, he/she must submit an authenticated or apostilled Certificate of Specialization. The validity/expiration date must be reflected on the professional license or certificate and it remains valid during the practice of profession in the Philippines. For professional licenses/registration with lifetime validity, the applicant is required to submit an updated Certificate of Good Standing (COGS) issued by the Professional Regulatory Authority (PRA) or Accredited Institution for the Profession from the applicant's country of origin. The same must be apostilled/authenticated.

Please see asterisk below on the legalization of the document. The laws are available at https://www.prc.gov.ph/professional-regulatory-boards.

*** LEGALIZATION OF DOCUMENT EXECUTED/ISSUED ABROAD: Starting 14 May 2019, foreign documents from Apostille-contracting countries (available at https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41) need not be authenticated abroad by Philippine Embassies and Consulates General in order to be recognized and accepted in the Philippines. Apostille Certification or e-Apostille (electronic copy) issued by the foreign competent authority responsible for the implementation of the Apostille Convention will be sufficient. While foreign documents issued in non-member countries including Germany, shall have notarial (i.e., acknowledgement and jurat) with authentication from the Philippine Embassies and Consulates. The document must be accompanied by an official English translation, if applicable.

4. For Categories STP1, STP2, and STP3, at least one (1) Filipino Professional counterpart for every foreign professional whose services will be engaged in the Philippines, who shall be employed for the same duration as the foreign national’s tenure with the company or firm; indicate the name of counterpart in the letter request supported by a contract of employment with a photocopy of current PRC Professional I.D. Card (The validity of the Professional ID Card must be within the duration of the practice of profession of the foreign national. However, with regard to the following:

Accountancy: If the foreign national is an ASEAN CPA, the counterpart should be a Filipino ASEAN CPA.

Electronics Engineering: There must be at least two (2) Filipino electronics engineer counterparts for every foreign professional.

Geodetic Engineering: The Filipino counterpart must be a member in good standing with the A.P.O.

Interior Design: The Filipino counterpart must be in continuous practice of interior design for at least ten (10) years).

5. For Category STP4:

At least one (1) Filipino Professional counterpart for every foreign professional whose services will be engaged in the Philippines to be indicated in the letter request to PRC/PRB with a photocopy of current PRC Professional I.D. However, with regard to Midwifery, Nutrition and Dietetics, Physical Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Respiratory Therapy and Veterinary Medicine, instead of providing a Filipino Professional counterpart, applicant must submit names of officers or representatives of local sponsoring organization/institution. This is not applicable to Agriculture, Chemistry and Social Workers.

At least one (1) Filipino Professional counterpart of the same specialization for every foreign dentist or physician-specialists, whose services are under co-management arrangement characterized by shared responsibility, authority, and accountability in patient care.

6. One (1) piece passport size I.D. picture in formal attire with complete name tag in white background

7. For profession specific documentary requirements, the same is available at https://prc.gov.ph/special-temporary-permits.

retrieval_text:
REQUEST FOR AN EXEMPTION OR EXCLUSION FROM THE STP REQUIREMENT

Requirement 1: Letter request addressed to PRC/PRB requesting for an exemption from authority to practice by citing clear factual and/or legal basis for an exemption
Requirement 2: Photocopy of valid passport as proof of citizenship
Requirement 3: Notarized copy of the Contract of Employment or Services, or Memorandum of Agreement between the employer and the foreign professional, indicating the terms of reference, nature of engagement, scope, duration and other project or contract details
